findings.description: The restart-required modal reminder can fire after a plugin-level configuration rejection, not only after a transport failure. The pinned host `Jellyfin.Api.Controllers.PluginsController.UpdatePluginConfiguration` always returns `NoContent()` (204) and `Plugin.UpdateConfiguration` swallows an invalid candidate (it does not persist and does not throw/signal), so the client promise resolves and the page's success callback runs `Dashboard.processPluginConfigurationUpdateResult(result)` followed by `showRestartRequiredReminder(restartRequiredChanged)`. The current-state architecture sentence and the task 16.5 changelog/report claim a rejected POST shows no reminder (the 16.4 spike even names the ADR-021 rejection as the example); that holds only for an HTTP/transport-level rejection, not for the ADR-021 config-validation rejection. It is a best-effort modal and the always-present note text and save behaviour are unaffected.
findings.detail: The reminder is correctly placed inside the successful `updatePluginConfiguration(...).then` callback and no rejection handler calls it, which is exactly what the 16.5 tests assert. The gap is the wording/assumption that the ADR-021 rejection rejects the POST: it does not. The pre-existing save path already shows the SettingsSaved toast on a rejected candidate (the rejection is surfaced only through the ADR-021 activity log), so the reminder adds a second signal consistent with that pre-existing gap rather than introducing a new state problem.
evidence: src/ArrTags/Plugin.cs:143-173 (invalid candidate is not persisted and does not throw; TryNotifyRejected)
docs/architecture/06-configuration-and-persisted-state.md:149-150 ("so a rejected POST shows no reminder")
docs/changelog/v1.2.0.md:607-609 ("a rejected POST shows no restart reminder")
docs/research/jellyfin-expert/modal-notification-api.json (recommendation names the ADR-021 rejection as the no-reminder case)
findings.recommended_action: Reword the current-state architecture-06 sentence (and any future report wording) to distinguish a transport/HTTP rejection from the ADR-021 config-validation rejection, or explicitly accept that a rejected candidate can still show the best-effort reminder. Changelog/implementation records are immutable history; correct only the current-state surface if the project wants the narrower claim. Not required for phase approval.

findings.description: `byteLimitToDisplay` in config.html renders a zero byte value as the empty string (the `(scaled/divisor).toFixed(P)` then trailing-zero/`.` trim removes all characters), while the mirrored C# `ByteLimitField.FormatDisplay(0)` returns "0". The edge is unreachable through validated configuration because every byte field's minimum is at least 1 KiB (4096 bytes) and an out-of-range persisted value is rejected at load. No action required.
findings.recommended_action: None for v1.2; a defensive `scaled === 0` branch could be added if the mapping ever gains a zero minimum.

findings.description: The reflection guard in RestartRequiredSettingsTests detects a newly added, entirely unclassified writable leaf property, but it cannot detect a future singleton that begins capturing an already-classified per-operation setting at construction (the setting would silently become misclassified). This is inherent to a static classification and is disclosed in the task 16.2 known limitations and ADR-028's consequence (adding a future limit requires classifying it).
evidence: docs/implementation/16.2/worker-report.attempt-2.json known_limitations (per-operation classification rests on cited consumer sites, not a per-setting mutation probe)
findings.recommended_action: No action for v1.2; keep the classification review as a maintained contract for future limit additions.

findings.description: The page's inline JavaScript (byte display/store conversion and the Dashboard.alert modal) is not executed by any test or by the pinned live matrix (--nowebclient); it is pinned structurally against the code-owned ByteLimitUnits/RestartRequiredSettings sources and the embedded page resource. The byte conversion itself is exercised as real C#. This residual is registered as accepted limitation V12-G8-1 (LOW) and is stated in the ADR-028 implementation note, README, test XML docs, and changelog rather than overclaimed.
evidence: docs/testing/jellyfin-12-musl-test-host.md (corrected: archive ships jellyfin-web/; --nowebclient means the live matrix does not serve it)
findings.recommended_action: No action; correctly registered and accurately bounded.

summary: Phase 16 (G6/G8, ADR-028) is complete and the six tasks 16.1-16.6 each have a commit, worker and reviewer evidence, and per-task orchestration records; the phase aggregate exists and is internally consistent except for its advisory cost figure (P16-F2). Independent inspection confirms the shipped code matches the documents: ByteLimitUnits/ByteLimitField implement the per-field fixed binary unit, step, precision, scaled-integer conversion, explicit step-multiple rejection, and trailing-zero-trimmed display; the mapping's bounds/defaults match the unchanged OperationalLimits.Validate (including the three 64 KiB minima at 0.0625 MB); the persisted XML and internal values stay bytes; RestartRequiredSettings classifies all 43 user-adjustable settings with the seven-setting restart-required set (three mixed, four construction-only) and per-consumer evidence that I spot-verified against the actual singleton constructors; every restart-required setting carries always-present static note text (mixed ones with the immediate-application clause); the modal reminder follows the 16.4 spike, runs only inside the accepted save callback, and fails open to the note text. The G6/G8 integration test composes the real dashboard POST deserialization, Plugin.UpdateConfiguration, and XML boundary, and all min/default/max round-trip exactly. Canonical documentation (architecture 06/12, data-model 03-12, README, ADR-028 implementation note, decisions index, limitations register V12-G6-1/V12-G8-1/V12-G8-2, musl test-host correction) is reconciled with no stale current-state claim, and the three registered limitations are accurately classified Accepted (all LOW/INFORMATIONAL; none hides an open BLOCKER/HIGH). check-docs passes, the generated surfaces are current, and phase 16 correctly remains PLANNED with tag v1.2.0-phase16 and no gate/tag applied. No BLOCKER or HIGH finding is open; the LOW/INFORMATIONAL findings (modal can fire after a plugin-level config rejection due to the ADR-021 silent-save path; aggregate cost mismatch; and inherent structural-only/static-classification limitations) do not block the phase or the next phase.
